specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** simulation-fit-judge
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Evaluate
**Bloom Verb:** judge
**Learning Objective:** The learner will judge whether a simulation or plain text serves each of eight learning goals better, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Interactive Simulation, MicroSim, Practice Problem (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each goal the learner commits one of two bins. A placement is correct when it matches the Correct bin column in Content. Mastery is at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. Reading the rule of thumb is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A simulation is always better than text. (2) A simulation is only for science. (3) Interactive means a game. **Instructional Rationale:** Judging the fit of a tool to a goal is an Evaluate-level action that a reviewer needs when deciding whether a resource lacks interactivity or is padded with it. Eight goals that split evenly teach the learner to apply one test to each. **Content:** The rule of thumb, shown at all times: a simulation helps when the learner needs to change a quantity and see an effect, or to practice a procedure with immediate feedback. Plain text suffices for fixed facts and definitions. The two bins: A simulation would help more, and Text or a table is enough. The eight goals: | # | Learning goal shown to the learner | Correct bin | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | See how changing a pendulum's length changes how fast it swings. | A simulation would help more | The learner changes a quantity and sees an effect. | | 2 | Memorize the names of the planets. | Text or a table is enough | It is a fixed list, and flash cards fit better than a simulation. | | 3 | Understand how paving changes runoff by changing the share of paved land. | A simulation would help more | The learner varies a quantity and watches runoff change. | | 4 | Read the definition of a watershed. | Text or a table is enough | A definition is a fixed statement. | | 5 | Explore how a savings rate changes the growth of savings over thirty years. | A simulation would help more | The learner varies a rate and sees the long-run effect. | | 6 | Learn the dates of five historical events. | Text or a table is enough | They are fixed facts. | | 7 | Practice balancing a chemical equation with immediate checking. | A simulation would help more | The learner practices a procedure and gets feedback at once. | | 8 | Find out who wrote a famous poem. | Text or a table is enough | It is a single fact. | **Provenance:** The goals are illustrative cases written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The rule of thumb follows the chapter sections "Interactive Simulation" and "MicroSim". **Rules:** Each goal has exactly one correct bin, four per bin. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one goal and the two bins. 2. The learner places the goal in a bin, and the placement is committed. 3. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 4. After goal 8 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 8 goals in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [bin]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. [bin]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 8 correct on the first attempt". At 7 or more it adds "You can tell when interactivity earns its place." Below 7 it lists the Why text of each missed goal. **Starting State:** The first goal and the two bins. The question shown is "Would a simulation teach this better than text?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter says a simulation suits ideas where the learner varies a quantity and sees an effect, or practices a procedure with feedback, and that plain text is better for a fixed fact or a definition.
